GeneralInformation.MappingName: pacs.008 to Core Banking System Conversion

BusinessContext.Description: Converts ISO 20022 pacs.008.001.08 (FIToFICustomerCreditTransfer) messages into Core Banking System transactions for account posting. This is the final step in the payment processing chain where the payment instruction is translated into actual debit/credit entries in customer and internal bank accounts. pacs.008 represents interbank credit transfers. When a bank receives such a message, it must credit the beneficiary customer account, update nostro/vostro accounts, post to General Ledger, generate account statements, and update balances. This mapping bridges the gap between the standardized ISO 20022 messaging layer and proprietary Core Banking systems such as Temenos T24, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra Equation, Mambu, and Thought Machine Vault.

UseCases.UseCase: Incoming international payment - credit customer account

BusinessContext.ApplicableDomains: Core Banking, Account Management, General Ledger, Nostro Reconciliation, Customer Accounts, Payment Operations, Real-time Payments

MappingFormula.PseudoCode: transaction_id = source.payment_id.transaction_id if (NOT is_valid_format(transaction_id)) then throw error "Invalid transaction ID format" endif if (exists_in_posted_transactions(transaction_id)) then throw error "Duplicate transaction - already posted" endif if (exists_in_processing_queue(transaction_id)) then throw error "Transaction already in processing - idempotency protection" endif return transaction_id

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Missing transaction ID - cannot ensure idempotency"
REJECT with error "Duplicate transaction ID - already posted within detection window"
WAIT for completion or REJECT based on processing status

General.ImpactIfFails: Double posting of same payment causes duplicate credit to beneficiary. Financial loss and customer confusion. Regulatory reporting duplication.
General.BusinessRationale: Transaction ID is the primary idempotency key. Without it, network retries or message replay attacks cause duplicate credits. Duplicate detection window of DUPLICATE_DETECTION_WINDOW_DAYS days covers all realistic retry scenarios.
General.PerformanceImpact: MEDIUM (distributed cache lookup for duplicate check - Redis ~1-5ms, database fallback ~20-50ms)
General.AuditRequirement: All transaction IDs logged with receipt timestamp, source message ID, and posting result. Required for SOX financial controls and payment investigation. Retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Idempotency protection mandatory per PSD2 Article 80 strong customer authentication requirements. Duplicate prevention required per SWIFT message standards and ISO 20022 business rules.
General.DataPrivacy: Transaction ID is operational identifier. No direct PII. Not subject to GDPR special protections but retained for AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years for regulatory compliance.
General.MigrationNote: pacs.008 TxId maps directly to core banking transaction_id. This is a clean 1:1 mapping with no transformation required - only validation and duplicate checking.
General.CachingStrategy: Posted transaction IDs cached in Redis for DUPLICATE_DETECTION_WINDOW_DAYS days for fast duplicate detection. Cache miss falls back to database query. Cache populated synchronously at posting time.

MappingFormula.Expression: IF is_local_iban(source.CdtrAcct_Id_IBAN, our_country_code) THEN account_number = extract_account_from_iban(source.CdtrAcct_Id_IBAN) ELSE REJECT "Beneficiary not our customer" ENDIF target.account_number = account_number
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: iban = source.creditor_account.iban if (NOT is_valid_iban(iban)) then throw error "Invalid IBAN format" endif country_code = substring(iban, 1, 2) our_bank_country = get_config("bank_country_code") if (country_code != our_bank_country) then throw error "Beneficiary account not held at this bank" endif account_number = extract_bban_from_iban(iban, country_code) account = core_banking.get_account(account_number) if (account is null) then throw error "Account not found: " + account_number endif if (account.status != "ACTIVE") then throw error "Account is closed or blocked" endif if (fuzzy_match(account.holder_name, source.creditor_name) < NAME_MATCH_MIN_SCORE) then flag_for_manual_review("Name mismatch score below threshold - potential fraud") endif return account_number

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Invalid creditor IBAN"
REJECT - route to nostro if we are intermediary
REJECT with error "Account inactive or blocked - cannot credit"
FLAG for manual fraud review AND proceed with hold
REJECT with error "Invalid account type for incoming credit"

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment credited to wrong account - financial loss, regulatory breach, and potential fraud facilitation. Recovery requires manual reversal and customer notification.
General.BusinessRationale: Beneficiary account is the destination of the payment. Wrong account = misposted payment. Name matching above NAME_MATCH_MIN_SCORE detects mule accounts and authorized push payment fraud. IBAN structure varies by country requiring country-specific parsing logic.
General.PerformanceImpact: HIGH (IBAN validation, account lookup, status check, name matching - total ~50-150ms including database call)
General.AuditRequirement: Account lookup result, name match score, and account status logged per transaction. Name mismatch flags retained for fraud investigation. Required AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years per SOX and AML regulations.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Account status verification prevents posting to frozen accounts subject to court orders or sanctions. Name matching required per PSD2 Confirmation of Payee (CoP) Article 89. Account type restriction prevents posting to loan or deposit accounts not designed for incoming transfers.
General.DataPrivacy: Beneficiary account number and name are highly sensitive PII and financial data. Encrypted in transit and at rest. Access logged. Name match score stored for fraud investigation but account number pseudonymized in non-production logs.
General.MigrationNote: IBAN structure varies by country: Germany DE 22 chars (2 country + 2 check + 8 bank + 10 account), France FR 27 chars, UK GB 22 chars. Extraction logic must be country-aware. Non-SEPA accounts may arrive without IBAN requiring proprietary account lookup.
General.CachingStrategy: Account details cached per session (not persisted) to avoid repeated database calls within same batch. Cache invalidated between batches to pick up account status changes.

Condition.ElseAction: N/A - pacs.008 is always a credit transfer by definition

Variable.name: PACS008_DIRECTION
Variable.description: pacs.008 always represents incoming credit to beneficiary - static constant

General.ImpactIfFails: Wrong direction posting - DEBIT instead of CREDIT. Funds removed from customer instead of added. Catastrophic financial and reputational impact.
General.BusinessRationale: pacs.008 (FIToFICustomerCreditTransfer) is by ISO 20022 definition a credit to the beneficiary. This is a static invariant for this message type. Hardcoding prevents any misconfiguration risk.
General.AuditRequirement: Transaction direction logged as standard field in audit record. Any deviation from CREDIT would be immediately detected by post-posting balance reconciliation.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Correct transaction direction is foundational to double-entry accounting integrity required by IFRS 9 and Basel III. Incorrect direction would corrupt GL entries and financial statements.
General.DataPrivacy: Transaction type is operational data. No PII. No GDPR restrictions.
General.MigrationNote: This is unique to the pacs.008 to Core Banking mapping. pacs.004 (payment return) would map to DEBIT. pacs.009 (financial institution credit transfer) would also map to CREDIT but to a different account type.

MappingFormula.Expression: IF source.InstdAmt != null THEN amount = source.InstdAmt_value currency = source.InstdAmt_Ccy ELSE amount = source.IntrBkSttlmAmt_value currency = source.IntrBkSttlmAmt_Ccy ENDIF account_currency = get_account_currency(account_number) IF currency != account_currency THEN fx_rate = get_fx_rate(currency, account_currency, value_date) amount = round(amount * fx_rate, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES) currency = account_currency ENDIF target.amount = amount
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: instd_amt = source.instructed_amount if (instd_amt != null) then amount = instd_amt.value currency = instd_amt.currency else amount = source.interbank_settlement_amount.value currency = source.interbank_settlement_amount.currency endif account = core_banking.get_account(account_number) account_currency = account.currency if (currency != account_currency) then fx_rate = fx_service.get_rate(from: currency, to: account_currency, date: value_date, type: "MID") if (fx_rate is null) then throw error "FX rate not available for " + currency + "/" + account_currency endif converted_amount = round(amount * fx_rate, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES) core_banking.log_fx_conversion(transaction_id, amount, currency, converted_amount, account_currency, fx_rate) amount = converted_amount currency = account_currency endif if (amount <= 0) then throw error "Amount must be positive after FX conversion" endif if (amount >= LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD AND AML_SCREENING_ENABLED) then aml_service.flag_for_review(transaction_id, amount, currency) endif return { amount: amount, currency: currency }

Condition.Action: USE_InstdAmt if present, fallback to IntrBkSttlmAmt
Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "No amount found in pacs.008 message"
REJECT with error "Amount must be strictly positive"
REJECT with error "FX rate not available - cannot convert " + currency + " to " + account_currency
FLAG for AML compliance review - amount exceeds LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD AND PROCEED
REJECT with error "Credit would exceed account maximum balance"

General.ImpactIfFails: Wrong amount posted causes financial discrepancy. FX conversion error causes exchange rate loss/gain dispute. Both require manual reversal and potential regulatory reporting.
General.BusinessRationale: Core financial value of the transaction. InstdAmt preferred over IntrBkSttlmAmt as it represents the original customer-facing amount before correspondent bank charges. FX conversion required for multi-currency accounts with rate cached FX_RATE_CACHE_TTL_MINUTES minutes for performance. AML threshold flagging mandatory for amounts above LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD.
General.PerformanceImpact: HIGH if FX conversion needed (external rate service call ~50-100ms). LOW for same-currency transactions (in-memory validation only). FX rate cache reduces repeated conversion latency to under 1ms.
General.AuditRequirement: All FX conversions logged with original amount, currency, converted amount, rate, and rate source per SOX financial controls. AML flags logged with transaction ID and threshold context. Amount logs retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Amounts above LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD must be flagged per EU 4th AML Directive Article 11. FX rate documentation required for audit per IFRS 9 fair value measurement rules. Amount precision limited to MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES to prevent rounding manipulation.
General.DataPrivacy: Transaction amounts combined with account data constitute sensitive financial information. Not PII per GDPR narrow definition but protected as financial confidential data with restricted access.
General.MigrationNote: ISO 20022 provides two amount fields: InstdAmt (customer's original amount) and IntrBkSttlmAmt (interbank settlement amount after charges). Core banking should credit InstdAmt to give customer full visibility. FX gain/loss from conversion posted to separate P&L GL account per IFRS 9.
General.CachingStrategy: FX rates cached in memory with FX_RATE_CACHE_TTL_MINUTES minute TTL. Cache refreshed from FX rate provider. Stale cache detected by TTL check. Same-currency transactions bypass cache entirely.

MappingFormula.Expression: settlement_date = source.IntrBkSttlmDt current_date = today() IF settlement_date > current_date THEN target.value_date = settlement_date target.booking_date = settlement_date target.status = "SCHEDULED" ELSE IF settlement_date == current_date THEN target.value_date = settlement_date target.booking_date = current_date target.status = "PENDING" ELSE IF days_back <= MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS THEN target.value_date = settlement_date target.booking_date = current_date target.status = "BACKDATED" ELSE REJECT "Backdate exceeds MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS allowed period" ENDIF ENDIF
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: value_date = source.interbank_settlement_date current_business_date = core_banking.get_business_date() if (NOT is_valid_date(value_date)) then throw error "Invalid settlement date format" endif if (NOT is_business_day(value_date)) then value_date = next_business_day(value_date) log_warning("Settlement date adjusted to next business day") endif if (value_date > current_business_date) then days_forward = value_date - current_business_date if (days_forward > MAX_FUTURE_DAYS) then throw error "Future value date exceeds MAX_FUTURE_DAYS maximum" endif booking_date = value_date transaction_status = "SCHEDULED" else if (value_date == current_business_date) then booking_date = current_business_date transaction_status = "PENDING" else days_back = current_business_date - value_date if (days_back > MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS) then throw error "Backdate of " + days_back + " days exceeds MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS maximum" endif booking_date = current_business_date transaction_status = "BACKDATED" audit.log_backdated_transaction(transaction_id, value_date, booking_date, days_back) endif return { value_date: value_date, booking_date: booking_date, status: transaction_status }

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Invalid settlement date"
ADJUST to next business day AND LOG warning
REJECT with error "Excessive backdating beyond MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS days"
REJECT with error "Future date exceeds MAX_FUTURE_DAYS days"

General.ImpactIfFails: Wrong value date causes incorrect interest accrual, regulatory reporting date errors, and customer balance availability issues. Excessive backdating creates audit risk.
General.BusinessRationale: Value date determines when funds earn interest and when the transaction appears in regulatory liquidity reports. MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS limit prevents date manipulation for regulatory arbitrage. Future-dated transactions scheduled for automated posting on value date.
General.PerformanceImpact: LOW (date arithmetic + business calendar lookup from in-memory cache)
General.AuditRequirement: All backdated transactions logged with original value date, booking date, number of days backdated, and approver. Backdating events reviewed by operations team. Required for central bank reporting accuracy audit.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Value date accuracy required for Basel III LCR reporting where payment date determines liquidity bucket. Backdating beyond MAX_BACKDATE_DAYS may require central bank notification in some jurisdictions. Business calendar validated against SWIFT market practice for each currency.
General.DataPrivacy: Settlement date is operational data. No PII. No GDPR restrictions.
General.MigrationNote: ISO 20022 IntrBkSttlmDt is in YYYY-MM-DD format (already converted). No date format transformation needed unlike MT103 YYMMDD conversion. Business day validation uses local market calendar loaded per currency at startup.
General.CachingStrategy: Business calendar cached per year and currency at startup. Holiday lists loaded from external provider. Cache refreshed annually and on ad-hoc holiday declarations.

MappingFormula.Expression: IF source.RmtInf_Ustrd != null THEN description = source.RmtInf_Ustrd ELSE description = "Credit transfer from " + source.Dbtr_Nm ENDIF target.description = truncate(description, 140) target.reference = source.EndToEndId
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: remittance_text = source.remittance_info.unstructured debtor_name = source.debtor.name end_to_end_ref = source.payment_id.end_to_end_id if (remittance_text != null AND remittance_text != "") then description = remittance_text else description = "Incoming payment from " + debtor_name endif if (length(description) > 140) then description = substring(description, 1, 137) + "..." endif reference = end_to_end_ref return { description: description, reference: reference }

Condition.ElseAction: TRUNCATE to 140 characters AND LOG truncation event
SANITIZE prohibited characters AND FLAG for AML review

Variable.name: STATEMENT_DESCRIPTION_MAX_LENGTH
Variable.description: Maximum characters for transaction description on customer statement

General.ImpactIfFails: Customer statement shows unclear transaction description. Manual reconciliation required. Corporate ERP invoice matching fails. Customer service calls increase.
General.BusinessRationale: Transaction description is the primary customer-facing text shown in online banking and statements. Rich remittance information enables automated invoice matching in corporate ERP systems reducing reconciliation effort by 60-80% for high-volume customers.
General.PerformanceImpact: NEGLIGIBLE (string manipulation only, no external calls)
General.AuditRequirement: Transaction description logged with audit record. Prohibited content flags logged separately for AML investigation. Truncation events logged for data quality monitoring.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Transaction narrative content screened for AML indicators (weapon keywords, sanctions-related terms) per bank AML policy. Prohibited character sanitization prevents XSS injection in online banking display.
General.DataPrivacy: Remittance text may contain PII (invoice to John Doe, personal reference numbers). Treated with same protections as name fields - encrypted in statement storage, access logged.
General.MigrationNote: ISO 20022 provides richer remittance options than MT103 field 70. Unstructured (Ustrd) maps directly to statement description. Structured (Strd) with ISO 11649 creditor references could enable more precise automated matching but requires additional parsing logic not yet implemented.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - pure string transformation per transaction.

MappingFormula.PseudoCode: originator_name = source.debtor.name originator_account = source.debtor_account.iban if (originator_name is null) then originator_name = "UNKNOWN" if (transaction_amount >= FATF_TRAVEL_RULE_THRESHOLD) then log_warning("Originator name missing for transaction above FATF threshold - compliance risk") endif endif return { originator_name: originator_name, originator_account: originator_account }

Condition.ElseAction: SET_TO_UNKNOWN AND LOG FATF Travel Rule compliance warning
REJECT with error "Originator name required for amounts above FATF_TRAVEL_RULE_THRESHOLD"

General.ImpactIfFails: FATF Travel Rule violation for transactions above FATF_TRAVEL_RULE_THRESHOLD. Potential regulatory fine. AML monitoring incomplete without originator information.
General.BusinessRationale: FATF Recommendation 16 (Travel Rule) requires originator name and account to accompany wire transfers above FATF_TRAVEL_RULE_THRESHOLD. Must be stored with transaction in core banking for AML monitoring, investigation, and regulatory reporting.
General.PerformanceImpact: NEGLIGIBLE (direct field copy with threshold check)
General.AuditRequirement: Originator name and account stored permanently with transaction. FATF Travel Rule compliance status logged per transaction. Missing originator flags reviewed by AML team. Retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years minimum.
General.ComplianceRequirement: FATF Recommendation 16 Travel Rule: originator name and account mandatory for transfers above FATF_TRAVEL_RULE_THRESHOLD. EU Wire Transfer Regulation 2015/847 implements this requirement. US Bank Secrecy Act 31 CFR 1010.410 equivalent rule.
General.DataPrivacy: Originator name and account are PII and financial data under GDPR. Encrypted in storage. Access restricted to AML, compliance, and investigation teams. Retained indefinitely for AML records despite GDPR right to erasure per Article 17(3)(b) AML exemption.
General.MigrationNote: pacs.008 already carries structured originator information in dedicated Dbtr (debtor) and DbtrAcct elements. No parsing or extraction needed - direct copy from ISO 20022 structured fields to core banking originator fields.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - originator data stored per transaction, not reused across transactions.

MappingFormula.PseudoCode: amount = transaction_amount currency = transaction_currency correspondent_bank = source.instructing_agent.bic if (account.type == "CHECKING") then customer_gl = GL_LIABILITY_RANGE_START + 100 else if (account.type == "SAVINGS") then customer_gl = GL_LIABILITY_RANGE_START + 200 endif nostro_gl = get_nostro_account(correspondent_bank, currency) entries = [] entries.add({ entry_id: generate_uuid(), transaction_id: transaction_id, gl_account: nostro_gl, debit_amount: amount, credit_amount: 0, currency: currency, value_date: value_date, description: "DR Nostro - Incoming pacs.008 from " + correspondent_bank }) entries.add({ entry_id: generate_uuid(), transaction_id: transaction_id, gl_account: customer_gl, debit_amount: 0, credit_amount: amount, currency: currency, value_date: value_date, description: "CR Customer " + account_number }) if (sum(entries.debit) != sum(entries.credit)) then throw error "GL entries not balanced - accounting integrity error" endif return entries

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Unbalanced GL entries - double-entry principle violated"
REJECT with error "Invalid GL account code - not in chart of accounts"
REJECT with error "GL account assigned to wrong range - accounting error"

General.ImpactIfFails: Financial statements corrupted. SOX audit failure. Basel III regulatory reporting errors. GL imbalance detected during EOD reconciliation causing statement delays.
General.BusinessRationale: Every bank transaction requires balanced double-entry GL posting per IFRS 9 and Basel III. Debit to nostro asset account (GL_ASSET_RANGE_START-GL_ASSET_RANGE_END range) represents funds received from correspondent. Credit to customer liability account (GL_LIABILITY_RANGE_START-GL_LIABILITY_RANGE_END range) represents bank obligation to customer. Balance equation always maintained.
General.PerformanceImpact: MEDIUM (GL account lookup from chart of accounts + balance validation - ~20-40ms including database validation)
General.AuditRequirement: All GL entries logged with transaction ID, account codes, debit/credit amounts, and posting timestamp. GL balance verification logged after each posting. Required for SOX Section 302/906 financial controls and external audit. Retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Double-entry accounting mandatory for licensed banks under Basel III Pillar 3 disclosure requirements. IFRS 9 financial instrument recognition requires accurate GL entries. SOX requires documented financial controls preventing unauthorized GL manipulation.
General.DataPrivacy: GL entries contain account numbers and amounts - financial confidential data. Not PII per GDPR but access restricted to finance, audit, and reconciliation teams. Encrypted at rest in GL database.
General.MigrationNote: GL account codes are institution-specific. Chart of accounts mapping (nostro per correspondent bank + currency, customer liability per account type) must be pre-configured per institution. FX conversion GL entries (P&L) added as additional entries when currency conversion occurs in MAPPING_04.
General.CachingStrategy: Chart of accounts cached in memory at startup. Nostro account mapping cached per correspondent BIC and currency. Cache refreshed when GL structure changes (typically quarterly).

MappingFormula.Expression: LOCK account FOR UPDATE WITH TIMEOUT ACCOUNT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS new_ledger_balance = account.ledger_balance + credit_amount new_available_balance = account.available_balance + credit_amount VALIDATE new_ledger_balance >= 0 AND new_ledger_balance <= account.maximum_balance UPDATE account balances UNLOCK account PUBLISH balance_updated event
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: account_number = transaction.account_number credit_amount = transaction.amount db.begin_transaction(isolation: DB_ISOLATION_LEVEL) retry_count = 0 while (retry_count < MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) do try { account = db.lock_for_update("accounts", account_number, timeout: ACCOUNT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) ledger_balance = account.ledger_balance available_balance = account.available_balance new_ledger_balance = ledger_balance + credit_amount new_available_balance = available_balance + credit_amount if (new_ledger_balance < 0) then throw error "Negative balance not allowed" endif if (new_ledger_balance > account.maximum_balance) then throw error "Maximum balance exceeded" endif account.ledger_balance = new_ledger_balance account.available_balance = new_available_balance account.last_credit_date = current_date() db.update(account) db.commit() event_bus.publish("BALANCE_UPDATED", { account_number: account_number, new_balance: new_ledger_balance }) alert_service.check_balance_alerts(account_number, new_ledger_balance) return { success: true, new_ledger_balance: new_ledger_balance } } catch (DEADLOCK or TIMEOUT) { db.rollback() retry_count = retry_count + 1 if (retry_count >= MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS) then throw error "Balance update failed after MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS retries" endif sleep(exponential_backoff(retry_count)) } catch (other_error) { db.rollback() throw other_error } end while

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Credit would result in negative balance"
REJECT with error "Credit would exceed maximum account balance"
RETRY up to MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS times with exponential backoff then REJECT

General.ImpactIfFails: Balance discrepancy between GL and account record. Customer cannot access credited funds. Overdraft protection may incorrectly reject subsequent debits.
General.BusinessRationale: Real-time balance update ensures customer has immediate access to credited funds. Pessimistic row-level locking (ACCOUNT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS timeout) prevents race conditions when concurrent transactions target same account. Exponential backoff retry up to MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS handles transient deadlocks without operator intervention.
General.PerformanceImpact: HIGH (row-level database lock + update + event publish - ~30-80ms under normal contention, up to ACCOUNT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS under high contention)
General.AuditRequirement: Balance before and after logged per transaction for SOX financial controls. Balance update events published to audit stream for real-time monitoring. Lock wait times monitored for performance alerting. Retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Real-time balance update required for PSD2 Account Information Service accuracy. Basel III LCR calculation requires accurate real-time balances. Pessimistic locking ensures ACID compliance per DB_ISOLATION_LEVEL isolation level.
General.DataPrivacy: Account balance is sensitive financial data. Not PII per GDPR narrow definition but access restricted to core banking systems, audit, and reconciliation. Balance history encrypted at rest.
General.MigrationNote: Balance update must be atomic with GL posting (MAPPING_08) within same database transaction to maintain GL-to-account consistency. If GL posting succeeds but balance update fails, automatic rollback of entire transaction prevents partial state.
General.CachingStrategy: Account balances NOT cached - always read from database under lock to prevent stale reads. Balance update events published to read-model cache (CQRS pattern) for read-heavy reporting queries.

MappingFormula.Expression: IF charge_bearer == "CRED" OR charge_bearer == "SHAR" THEN fees = calculate_fees(transaction_type: "INCOMING_WIRE", amount: amount, customer_segment: account.segment) IF fees.total > 0 THEN target = { fee_type: "INCOMING_WIRE_FEE", fee_amount: fees.total, charge_to_account: account_number } ENDIF ELSE target = null ENDIF
MappingFormula.PseudoCode: charge_bearer = source.charge_bearer amount = transaction_amount account = customer_account fee_schedule = FEE_SCHEDULE_SERVICE.get_fees( transaction_type: "INCOMING_INTERNATIONAL_WIRE", customer_segment: account.customer_segment ) if (account.customer_segment == FEE_WAIVER_SEGMENT) then return null endif if (fee_schedule.type == "FLAT") then fee_amount = fee_schedule.amount else if (fee_schedule.type == "PERCENTAGE") then fee_amount = max(fee_schedule.minimum, min(fee_schedule.maximum, amount * fee_schedule.percentage)) endif if (charge_bearer == "CRED" OR charge_bearer == "SHAR") then if (fee_amount > 0 AND account.available_balance >= fee_amount) then fee_transaction = { transaction_id: transaction_id + "_FEE", fee_type: "INCOMING_WIRE", fee_amount: fee_amount, charge_to_account: account_number, revenue_gl_account: GL_REVENUE_RANGE_START + 100 } return fee_transaction endif endif return null

Condition.Action: CALCULATE and APPLY fee to beneficiary
Condition.ElseAction: SKIP fee posting - sender pays (DEBT) or no charge
SKIP fee - segment FEE_WAIVER_SEGMENT is exempt from incoming wire fees
WAIVE fee to avoid overdraft AND LOG revenue exception
USE_DEFAULT_FEE_SCHEDULE and LOG missing configuration

General.ImpactIfFails: Revenue loss if fee not charged. Customer dispute if incorrect fee applied. GL revenue account not credited causing financial reporting gap.
General.BusinessRationale: Incoming wire fee is primary revenue source from correspondent banking. Fee waived for FEE_WAIVER_SEGMENT segment to retain high-value relationships. Charge bearer CRED or SHAR means beneficiary pays. DEBT means sender already covered fees - no charge to our customer.
General.PerformanceImpact: MEDIUM (fee schedule lookup + available balance check - ~20-40ms including cache lookup)
General.AuditRequirement: All fee calculations logged with schedule version, segment, calculation method, and result. Fee waivers logged with waiver reason (segment exemption or insufficient balance). Revenue GL entries auditable per SOX financial controls. Retained AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Fee transparency required per PSD2 Article 45 (payment service charges disclosure). Fee schedule must be published to customers in advance. Waived fees logged to prevent regulatory accusation of undisclosed charges.
General.DataPrivacy: Fee amount linked to account number is financial data. Not PII per GDPR but restricted access. Fee revenue reports pseudonymized to remove account-level detail for analytics.
General.MigrationNote: pacs.008 ChrgBr element maps cleanly to fee decision logic: CRED (creditor/beneficiary pays) and SHAR (shared) both trigger fee on our customer. DEBT (debtor/sender pays all) and SLEV (follow service level) skip beneficiary fee. Fee schedule must be maintained per customer segment and transaction type in separate configuration system.
General.CachingStrategy: Fee schedules cached per customer segment and transaction type at startup. Refreshed when pricing changes. Individual fee calculation results not cached - always computed fresh to reflect current schedule.
